title: Reference hardware verification (desktop + phone)
description: Run the full performance suite (transition hitches, render benchmark, tick benchmark, load smoke) on the reference desktop and the reference phone, and record the official v1 performance numbers — the gate that signs off SC-3 and SC-4.
acceptanceCriteria: Reference hardware is defined (documented in the report): desktop = a mid-2020s laptop (e.g., M2/Intel i5 class, integrated or entry-GPU, 16 GB) — the 'reference desktop'; phone = a mid-range 2023+ phone (8 GB, mid SoC) — the 'reference phone'; if a specific device is unavailable, the closest available one is used and named in the report (no silent substitution)

On the reference desktop: the transition benchmark (TASK-30) passes its 4 ms budget; the render benchmark (TASK-58) holds 60 fps (median ≤ 16.7 ms, p95 ≤ 20 ms, no > 50 ms frames) in the 16-entity worst case at the High preset; the tick benchmark (TASK-60) holds p95 < 30 ms; the load smoke (TASK-18) holds the snapshot rate + RTT rules

On the reference phone: the Mobile profile (TASK-59) holds ≥ 30 fps (median ≤ 33 ms) in the render benchmark's reduced scene (the 16-entity worst case, Mobile profile, no atmosphere dome); the full keyboard-only loop (TASK-54, Mobile forced) completes without a dropped frame > 100 ms

The report (docs/performance.md): a table per benchmark × device: {metric, budget, measured, pass/fail, device, date, git sha}; the SC-3 (60 fps desktop) and SC-4 (30 fps mobile floor) verdicts stated explicitly from the table
Any FAIL is a blocker: the failing benchmark's owning task is re-opened (a follow-up task is NOT created here — the fix goes back to the owner); the report lists each fail with its owner task id

The suite is runnable by a human in < 30 min per device: a single script npm run perf:report <device-tag> that runs the four benchmarks + the phone loop (phone via a Chrome remote-debugging connection or a local Android build — whichever is available in the environment; if phone testing is impossible in this environment, the phone section is marked BLOCKED-PENDING-DEVICE with the exact commands to run later, and SC-4 is reported as UNVERIFIED, not passed)
Report committed; all desktop numbers recorded; phone numbers recorded or the explicit BLOCKED note present; npm run test green (the unit/e2e suites pass on the dev machine as before)

steps.details: Identify the available desktop (the dev machine if it matches the reference class, else the closest + note); attempt the phone (Android via ADB/remote debugging, or iOS via Safari remote inspection — document the method); if no phone is reachable, prepare the exact commands + the BLOCKED note for later.
npm run perf:report desktop — runs: bench:transitions (TASK-30), bench:render (TASK-58), bench:tick (TASK-60), load:smoke (TASK-18); collect the JSON outputs; assemble the report table.
Same script tagged phone (the Mobile profile forced, the reduced render scene, the keyboard-only loop); if blocked, write the BLOCKED section with commands.

docs/performance.md per the acceptance format; the SC-3/SC-4 verdicts; any FAILs listed with owner task ids (those tasks stay open — this task does not close them); commit the report + the perf:report script.

technicalNotes: This task is measurement + reporting, not fixing: if something fails, the owner task is re-opened (the PRD's success criteria are signed off here and only here).
The perf:report script makes the verification repeatable for post-v1 hardware — it is infrastructure, not a one-off.
A BLOCKED-PENDING-DEVICE phone section is an honest outcome; a fabricated pass is not.
